failures.criterion: Copies are never lowered and a program that sets no byte limit never removes one (plan decisions 3 and 7; spec: a stream update keeps three copies and the byte limit) - with programs of one deployment starting at the same moment with different settings
failures.evidence: Real binaries on three nats-server v2.15.1 processes. The deployed stream is R1 with an older subject list, so every start updates it. One program has ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS=3 ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES=2000000. The other has neither setting (Dispatch's default; gcp:Dispatch takes both 'unset unless given'). Both start at the same moment. `bash /legion/scratch/tmp/t546/race.sh <workspace> 4 75` keeps both running for 75 s, then reads the stream. At 0681b121, 7 of 8 pairs (listener||listener and envoy-dispatch||listener) end with {"replicas":1,"max_bytes":-1}, both programs alive, buckets at 3: https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/2362#issuecomment-6434935100 . Earlier runs: tF 2/3, tK-M 2/4, tD 3/3 (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/2362#issuecomment-6434575953). Cause: the unset program reads the stream before the raise and writes its subject update after the raise, carrying R1 and no limit. JetStream's stream update has no compare-and-swap. The code comment accepts this race only on the condition of one value per deployment, but the CHANGELOG, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and the setting descriptions state the guarantee without that condition. Test 3i covers same-setting raisers only. The INFRA-14 architect decided (Envoy, 2026-10-27T05:31Z, sent to the implementer): (c). The docs make the guarantee conditional on one value per deployment, and a program that has the settings re-checks the stream and buckets at least once a minute and raises any that it finds lowered. Acceptance: race.sh ends, within one period after both starts, with three copies, the byte limit and the id in every round. No red Go test was committed: where the periodic re-check lives (bus.Client, or each program's main loop) is the implementer's design, and cmd/listener's main() has no in-process entry that a test could start. The red check is the real-binary harness race.sh (RESULT: FAIL at this head), which the next test round runs.
